title: Gaia DR3 eclipsing binaries match 10 TESS planet candidates in period and epoch; these TOIs are probable nearby-binary false positives (8151 TOIs, 3 arcmin search)
abstract: Question: Do faint nearby eclipsing binaries (EBs) that Gaia DR3 catalogued cause some TESS planet candidates? Approach: For 8151 TESS Objects of Interest (TOIs), we found all Gaia DR3 EBs within 3 arcmin (4591 pairs). We tested if the TOI period is equal to the EB period multiplied by a small ratio (relative deviation < 1e-3). We also tested if the TOI transit epoch agrees with the propagated Gaia eclipse time (phase gap < 0.05). We did the same search around control positions 0.5 deg away. Results: The TOI cones gave 132 period and epoch matches. The control cones gave 0. Matches occur for 121 of 604 (20%) known false positives that have an EB in the cone, and for 0 of 226 confirmed or known planets. Eleven TOIs with the disposition PC match. For 10 of them, the EB is a separate star 4.5 to 16 arcsec away, and its Gaia eclipse is deep enough to make the TESS signal after dilution. These are probable nearby-eclipsing-binary false positives: TOI 2998.01, 3063.01, 2541.01, 3258.01, 3143.01, 4870.01, 1960.01, 4876.01, 1546.01 and 5008.01. For TOI 1546.01 (a 3 Earth-radius candidate on a T = 9.9 star), ZTF photometry independently gives the EB period of 1.1328272 d and a 0.6 mag eclipse 0.41 h from the TOI epoch. TESS difference images put the signal on the EB for TOI 1960.01 and 2541.01. They put the signal on the target for two wide period-only matches (TOI 699.01 and 6496.01), so those matches are chance coincidences. For TOI 3142.01, the EB is the target star, which puts the signal on the target. Limitations: Gaia DR3 contains only a subset of EBs. Eight of the ten probable false positives have separations below 0.55 TESS pixels, so the TESS pixel data cannot resolve them. Gaia epoch photometry was not available during this work. Follow-up photometry is necessary for a final disposition.

display.caption: (a) Relative period deviation between TOIs and Gaia DR3 EBs within 3 arcmin, for TOI cones and offset control cones. (b) Epoch phase gap for period matches: TOI matches gather near zero; control matches do not. (c) Undiluted EB depth needed to make the TOI depth versus the Gaia G eclipse depth.

TESS FFI difference-image S/N maps. TOI 2541.01 and 1960.01 (Tier A): the signal is on the Gaia EB (green x). TOI 6496.01 and 699.01 (period-only matches): the signal is on the target (yellow circle), so these matches are chance coincidences.

ZTF photometry of Gaia DR3 384251315018012800, 10.8 arcsec from TOI 1546.01. BLS gives P = 1.1328272 d (Gaia 1.132826 d), which agrees with the TOI period of 1.13345 +- 0.0006 d. The fold on the ZTF ephemeris shows a 0.6 mag eclipse. The TOI epoch is 0.41 h from the predicted eclipse.
